transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-25 16:30 PDT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (Head of Search, Cobalt), Tom Becker (ML Eng), Amita Suresh (Infra Lead), Jamal Ortiz (CTO)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
Cobalt Research is evaluating Redwood for embeddings + rerank pipeline. They currently run a hybrid BM25 + vector pipeline on SoA, considering moving most reranking/embedding storage to an external vector DB. Primary concerns: throughput at peak (10k qps internal), embedding dimensionality and storage costs (512/768/1536 tradeoffs), latency SLO (~75-150ms p90 for first-pass + rerank), security/VPC and SOC2/KMS compliance. Redwood AE/SE discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options, fallback strategies (Faiss local shard, Redwood cache), and next steps include sharing pricing, SOC2 docs, and running a focused throughput microbenchmark with sample data.

Topics covered:
- Current search stack and hybrid retrieval approach
- Embedding dims and model tradeoffs (cost vs recall)
- Vector DB options and integration patterns (milvus, pinecone, self-hosted faiss)
- Throughput, batching, quantization, and latency/cost tradeoffs
- Deployment modes: Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved pools vs Private VPC
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO, RBAC

[00:00] Maya: "Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Sound check? Can you hear us okay?"
[00:05] Elena: "Yeah loud and clear. Thanks, Maya. Sorry for the late afternoon timing."
[00:09] Maya: "No worries. Quick intros, we have Ravi on the line who'll go deep on perf/cost, and I'll run the commercial context. You want to intro Cobalt folks?"
[00:15] Jamal: "Sure, I'm Jamal, CTO, and Elena runs the search team. Tom is our ML engineer handling embeddings and ranking, Amita handles infra. We're evaluating options to lower latency and cost on our research portal."
[00:26] Maya: "Great. High level: are you evaluating Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments? Or all three?"
[00:31] Elena: "All three for now - short list is Redwood Hosted for quick start, Dedicated for guaranteed throughput, Private for regulatory customers. We need to understand tradeoffs especially when we roll to 10k qps internal peaks."
[00:42] Ravi: "Makes sense. Before we jump in, can you share current numbers? Primary query QPS, average doc size, embedding dim and current vector DB?"
[00:51] Tom: "We're doing about 1k steady qps but spikes to 8-12k during experiments. Docs are fairly small — 1-3KB per doc. Using 768 dims right now, model is an in-house finetuned embedder but we've also prototyped with OpenAI and a 1536 variant. For vector store we're currently on an in-house Faiss cluster with some sharding; looking at Milvus and managed options for simpler ops."
[01:17] Ravi: "Ok, good context. Two main knobs to trade: embedding dimensionality and model vs quantization, and routing/batching to meet latency SLO. For 10k spikes you probably need Dedicated reserved capacity or Private with autoscale tooling. Hosted can work for baseline but you'd need burst policies."
[01:35] Amita: "We prefer not to run our own GPU fleet if we can avoid it. Ops overhead is a blocker. But data residency and strict network policies might push us to Private."
[01:45] Maya: "Totally. Quick note on costs: moving from 768 -> 1536 roughly doubles token/embedding compute cost for model generation, but you may get recall gains; Redwood Optimize can suggest 2/3 quantization (int8) and hybrid rerank to save costs. Ravi, maybe walk them through a typical pipeline?"
[01:59] Ravi: "Sure. Typical flow: first-pass BM25 or fast vector k-NN at low dims for recall, then a lightweight reranker model or cross-encoder for top-K reordering. If you keep embeddings at 768, you get smaller storage and faster nearest-neighbor retrieval; 1536 helps for edge-case recall but costs more. With Redwood's runtime we can do prefix KV cache and ELR batching so the per-token latency stays low. Important: batch size choices change p95 by tens of ms depending on sequence lengths.
[02:30] Elena: "Can you explain how caching works with a vector DB? We currently don't have good prefix caching on Faiss."
[02:36] Ravi: "Sure — prefix/KV cache is mostly for decoder-based generation not retrieval, but for retrieval we can use result caching: frequently asked queries' neighbor lists can be cached in Redwood or a front cache like Redis. For dedicated clusters, we support hot shard pinning and local Faiss in the same VPC, reducing network hop. There's also automatic fallback to smaller model variants when latency spikes."
[02:58] Tom: "What's the typical p95 for a two-stage pipeline — first pass k-NN (512-768d) plus cross-encoder rerank? Our target is 75-150ms end-to-end."
[03:08] Ravi: "If you use a lightweight faiss/Milvus vector lookup in <20ms for k-NN and a small cross-encoder rerank (on a 2-3 token avg context) you can be sub-150ms p95 on Dedicated with 8-16 batch window, but Hosted latencies vary depending on multi-tenant load. The big variable is reranker model size — a medium cross-encoder adds 40-80ms typically."
[03:35] Jamal: "Latency's critical. We can't have user-facing search slower than 200ms on p95. We also need predictable unit economics — storage and per-embedding cost across millions of docs matters."
[03:45] Maya: "Right. For storage we show cost per 1M vectors at 768 vs 1536 and also compression options — int8 or product quantization can cut storage 4x with some recall drop. We'll include that spreadsheet.
[03:58] Elena: "On the vector DB front, our concerns: operational complexity, backups/snapshots, and also sharding strategy for geo distribution. Do you have customers who've done Milvus + Redwood?"
[04:09] Ravi: "Yes, several. Integration patterns: 1) Redwood as the model/runtime with embeddings stored in Milvus/Pinecone; Redwood calls the vector DB for k-NN then handles rerank internally. 2) Redwood-hosted embeddings + integrated nearest neighbor — less moving parts but more network egress if Private. We can also run a colocated Faiss instance in Redwood Dedicated clusters for lower latency."
[04:34] Tom: "Any preferred route for hybrid search? We want BM25 + vector fusion, then rerank. We're debating whether to compute dense-only top 100 and fuse with BM25 or first BM25 top 500 then do vector intersection."
[04:47] Ravi: "Both are valid. Common pattern: BM25 to get recall for rare tokens, take top-N (500), embed those doc candidates and do vector re-rank. If DB supports hybrid scoring you can do weighted fusion. The cost tradeoffs: embedding 500 docs is heavier but often yields better final relevance. Redwood Optimize can recommend thresholds based on your query distributions."
[05:10] Amita: "What about private deployment network setup? We use strict egress rules and need KMS integration for keys. Also SSO via SAML is required."
[05:19] Maya: "For Private we support customer-managed VPCs with private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO, and audit logs. We'll share the security pack. There's a small on-boarding window for peering. Ravi, add a note on peering latency considerations."
[05:32] Ravi: "Peering latency matters: colocating the vector DB in the same VPC reduces request time. If using a managed vector DB across regions you'll see higher variance, which affects p95. For on-prem, we can ship a package but operations are more hands-on."
[05:47] Elena: "We'd like to pilot with hosted then move to Dedicated if results are good. Are there quickstart projects you recommend?"
[05:55] Maya: "Yes, we typically do a 2-4 week pilot where we ingest a 10k doc subset, run batch embeddings, run throughput tests at target qps and a rerank eval. We'll provide a benchmark harness and a simple cost model. Ravi will partner on perf tests."
[06:10] Tom: "For embedding dims — any empirical guidance? Our recall drop from 768->512 was noticeable on some queries."
[06:18] Ravi: "Empirically: 768 is a good middle ground for many tasks. 512 may lose semantic nuances, 1536 improves nuance but double cost. Another lever is using lightweight 768 embeddings for retrieval and a heavier 1536 vector for rerank embedding on small candidate sets — but that requires extra embedding compute on top-K docs."
[06:40] Jamal: "Can Redwood handle on-demand embedding upscaling for rerank? Like generate 768 repo vectors at ingest and then compute 1536 for top candidates at query time?"
[06:49] Ravi: "Yes — Redwood supports mixed model flows. You can store 768 at ingest; at query time call a larger cross-encoder or generate on-the-fly 1536 embeddings for top candidates. The tradeoff is query-time compute. With Dedicated you can keep predictability."
[06:59] Elena: "What are typical fallback strategies if Dedicated hits capacity?"
[07:06] Maya: "We have policy-based routing: fallback to lower-cost model variant, route to alternate region or degrade to BM25-only for a brief period. Redwood's console shows token-level cost and you can set automated fallback thresholds."
[07:19] Amita: "Any gotchas with Faiss shards and autoscaling? We saw issues previously — rebalancing was disruptive."
[07:26] Ravi: "Sharding rebalances are non-trivial; managed solutions like Milvus or Pinecone handle that better. Our Dedicated offering has tooling to orchestrate shard moves with minimal impact — but it's something to plan for during growth windows."
[07:40] Tom: "For the microbenchmark, what do you need from us?"
[07:44] Ravi: "Sample query log (anonymized), doc subset (~10k), target qps profile (steady vs spiky), and desired latency SLO. We'll run vector k-NN + rerank scenarios and produce p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M queries estimates."
[07:59] Elena: "We'll put that together. I also want the SOC2 docs and network diagram to share with our security team."
[08:05] Maya: "We'll send the security pack. Note: Hosted customers get SOC2 but for Private we have additional paperwork for data residency. I'll include a checklist."
[08:14] Jamal: "What's the timeline for moving from pilot to Dedicated?"
[08:18] Maya: "Customary path: 2-4 week pilot, then if metrics meet thresholds we convert to a Dedicated commit — typical procurement takes 2-6 weeks depending on enterprise approvals. We'll help with procurement docs."
[08:29] Tom: "Any existing customers with a similar qps profile you can reference?"
[08:32] Ravi: "Yes, a fintech customer runs ~12k spike QPS with Dedicated plus pre-warmed burst; they use a mix of BM25 + vector and keep a cross-encoder rerank. I'll add that case study link in the follow-up."
[08:46] Elena: "One more question — embeddings lifecycle: if we re-index models often, how do you manage vector updates without big downtime?"
[08:54] Ravi: "Blue/green reindexing is common: index into new shards, swap pointers after validation. For managed stores we can do zero-downtime swaps. We'll share patterns we've used with Faiss and Milvus."
[09:10] Amita: "Operational question — what's the visibility into per-request costs? We want to attribute costs to product lines."
[09:16] Maya: "Redwood Console provides token/embedding level breakdowns per route, and you can tag routes so cost shows up per product. That helps with chargeback."
[09:27] Jamal: "Ok if we do a pilot on Hosted first, how easy to migrate to Dedicated? Data movement costs?"
[09:33] Ravi: "We provide migration tooling; the main cost is re-ingesting embeddings into Dedicated store or exporting vectors. If you store raw embeddings in your vector DB, migration is mostly pointer reconfiguration with a one-time sync."
[09:46] Elena: "Thanks. This was very helpful. Next steps: we'll get Tom to drop the sample dataset and query logs, and we'll expect the pricing/security docs."
[09:55] Maya: "Perfect. I'll send pricing, SOC2/KMS docs, and the benchmark plan. Ravi will draft the microbenchmark script and timeline. Any final questions?"
[10:04] Tom: "Quick nit — can Redwood integrate with our existing SSO and provision RBAC for engineers only?"
[10:09] Maya: "Yes, SAML/SCIM support and granular RBAC. We'll include that in the security pack."
[10:15] Jamal: "Thanks everyone. We'll follow up after we assemble the artifact bundle."
[10:19] Maya: "Thanks all, we'll follow up by end of week with documents and proposed dates for perf run. Bye."
